jobs.title: Director and Practice Lead, Data Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital agency and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture.

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across: Digital Product Strategy & Innovation, Digital Marketing Services, Web & Mobile App Development, Data & AI, Cloud Engineering, and Enterprise Technology Modernization.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

Our Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering
will operate remotely in Canada OR be based out of either our Toronto, ON or Vancouver, BC office locations.

The Opportunity

TELUS Digital's Data, AI & Cloud (DAIC) practice is the multidisciplinary engine behind enterprise AI, blending boutique innovation with the breadth of a global services portfolio to help organizations architect, scale, and secure their transformations. Spanning our full family of specialized capabilities, the DAIC practice delivers end-to-end solutions across AI Advisory, AI Solutions, Data & AI Platforms, and Cloud Transformation.

As a premier Google Cloud partner, our Cloud practice is at the forefront of helping enterprises adopt and scale on Google Cloud infrastructure: delivering complex engineering, deployment, and migration programs for some of the largest organizations in Canada and beyond.

The Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering
will define and own the Data Engineering Practice along with its market positioning, P&L, talent, and the quality of work we deliver for clients. This role is for someone who has led data and AI practices before, understands how to turn messy enterprise data estates into strategic assets, and earns trust with C-suite executives through genuine expertise. You will shape how we help clients move from data ambition to durable, AI-ready infrastructure.

This Role Will Have Four Core Anchor Responsibilities

Strategy: Set the practice vision and align Data & AI capabilities to where enterprise demand is heading.
P&L: Own revenue targets, margin, and growth while being accountable for the practice's full commercial performance.
Talent & Culture: Build a practice where data-driven thinking, innovation, and engineering rigour are the baseline.
Client Impact: Act as a trusted advisor to enterprise CxOs navigating data strategy, AI adoption, and governance.

Responsibilities

Define the multi-year vision for the Data Engineering Practice, ensuring our technical capabilities are ahead of the curve for enterprise demand for Data & AI transformation.
Own the full P&L, including pipeline, pricing, delivery margin, and revenue growth, while reporting directly to executive leadership with clear commercial accountability.
Build and sustain senior relationships with Google Cloud partner teams and client executives to generate meaningful deal flow and expand strategic accounts.
Lead the practice's position on ethical AI and data democratisation while making principled, evidence-based bets on where advanced analytics and AI are creating real enterprise value.
Drive investment in reusable IP, data accelerators, and delivery assets that improve consistency, reduce time-to-value, and protect margins at scale.
Serve as a strategic advisor to client C-suite executives, helping them define data strategy, navigate AI adoption, and build the organisational capabilities to sustain it.
Set the standard for engineering and analytical excellence across the practice by hiring well, developing talent deliberately, and building teams that clients trust and return to.

Competencies

12+ years in data or AI consulting, including at least 3–5 years in a practice leadership or executive role, not just senior delivery or individual contribution.
Proven P&L ownership: Direct experience managing revenue, margin, and growth targets in a consulting or professional services context.
Data and AI ecosystem depth: Strong command of modern data architecture, AI, and ML trends, cloud-native data platforms, and enterprise data governance.
Executive communication: Able to advise, challenge, and build lasting trust with C-suite stakeholders on complex, ambiguous problems, not just present to them.
Business Development track record: Experience generating pipeline and closing complex, multi-stakeholder engagements, not just managing delivery once work is sold.
Talent leadership: Has hired, grown, and retained senior data engineering and consulting talent in a practice or delivery organisation.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At TELUS Digital, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

For more information on how we use your information, see our Privacy Policy.

Classification & Regular Hours

The base salary will be $100,000 - $125,000 per annum. Starting salary will be aligned with the successful candidate’s experience, skills, and demonstrated qualifications.

About Western

Since 1878, Western University has been committed to serving our communities through the pursuit of academic excellence and by providing students, faculty, and community members with life-long opportunities for intellectual, social, and cultural growth. We seek excellent students, faculty, and staff to join us in what has become known as the "Western Experience" - an opportunity to contribute to a better world through the development of new knowledge, new abilities, new connections, and new ways to make a difference.

About Us

The Western Advancement division plays a leading role in strengthening awareness of and support for the University’s mission and goals by leading alumni relations and fundraising efforts across campus and beyond. All departments within the Division build enduring alumni and public trust through understanding and support for Western University in a coordinated campus-wide effort that results in the engagement and funding needed to make an impact. There are 3 departments within the Division – Departments of Development, Alumni Relations and Advancement Operations.

The Advancement Operations department is a partner in the areas of constituent database and technology services, prospect management, research and pipeline, data analytics and storytelling, gift and pledge management, records and document management, and financial reconciliation and reporting. In addition, we provide support to the annual planning process as well as budget management, talent management and facilities support for Western Advancement.

An integral part of Advancement Operations, the Technology team is responsible for the strategic leadership, management and optimization of systems, data and technology solutions that support fundraising, alumni engagement and operational priorities. The unit ensures the reliability, security, integrity and effective use of technology infrastructure, hardware, software applications and information resources across Western Advancement. The team provides leadership in website development and management, e-commerce platforms, digital communications, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, business intelligence and analytics, data governance and technical support. Through collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, the unit identifies business requirements, develops innovative technology solutions, delivers user training and supports data-driven decision making to enhance alumni and donor engagement.

Responsibilities

The Director, Technology (Western Advancement) provides strategic leadership for the technology, systems, information management, business intelligence and digital capabilities that enable Western Advancement's fundraising, alumni engagement, and operational activities. As a member of the Advancement Operations leadership team, the Director works collaboratively with leaders and colleagues across Western Advancement, Western Technology Services, Office of the Registrar and other related units to understand evolving business needs, establish technology priorities, and develop innovative and forward-looking strategies and solutions that strengthen operational effectiveness, enhance the constituent experience, and advance Western's fundraising and engagement priorities.

The Director leads the development and implementation of Western Advancement's technology strategy and roadmap, providing leadership for a multidisciplinary team responsible for systems and software applications, data management, business intelligence and analytics, web and digital applications, technical training, and end-user technology services. The role provides strategic oversight for Western Advancement's technology ecosystem, identifies opportunities to innovate, improve and integrate systems and technology business processes, and establishes priorities for technology investments, projects, services, and resources. Working in close partnership with Western Technology Services and other University partners, the Director ensures technology solutions are reliable, secure, sustainable, and aligned with institutional standards while positioning Western Advancement to respond effectively to emerging needs, opportunities, and technologies.

Qualifications

Education:
Undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, Technology Management, or another related discipline
Master’s degree in Business Administration, Information Systems, Technology Management, or another related discipline preferred
Professional certification in project management, information technology governance, information security, business analysis, or another related area is considered an asset

Experience:
7 years’ progressively responsible experience leading technology, information systems, digital solutions, or technology-enabled business operations within a large, complex organization
Experience developing and implementing technology strategies, roadmaps, governance frameworks, and investment priorities that align technology capabilities with organizational objectives
Experience leading multidisciplinary technology teams and functions, including responsibility for human, financial, operational, and technology resources
Experience evaluating complex business requirements and developing technology, systems, integration, and process solutions that improve organizational effectiveness and service delivery
Experience developing and managing technology budgets, contracts, vendor relationships, and resource plans, including evaluating technology investments and making strategic recommendations
Experience leading technology services within advancement, fundraising, alumni relations, higher education, or another complex relationship-based organization preferred
Experience with advancement technology ecosystems, constituent relationship management systems, fundraising and engagement platforms, business intelligence and analytics, or related technologies preferred
Experience working within a decentralized technology environment requiring collaboration with enterprise technology functions and multiple organizational units preferred

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:
Comprehensive knowledge of technology strategy, information systems, systems integration, technology governance, service delivery, and contemporary technology management practices
Demonstrated ability to translate complex organizational and business requirements into forward-looking technology strategies, priorities, solutions, and implementation approaches
Strong business acumen and strategic thinking skills with the ability to evaluate technology opportunities and investments in relation to organizational priorities, business value, risk, resource requirements, and long-term sustainability
Demonstrated knowledge of information security, privacy, accessibility, business continuity, technology risk management, and system lifecycle considerations within a complex organizational environment
Demonstrated knowledge of data and information management, business intelligence, analytics, and the role of technology in enabling reliable information and informed organizational decision-making
Exceptional leadership and people management skills with the ability to establish strategic direction, integrate multidisciplinary functions, develop professional capabilities, allocate resources, and foster a collaborative and high-performing team environment
Exceptional consultation, relationship management, and influencing skills with the ability to establish credibility, understand diverse business needs, build consensus, and develop effective partnerships with senior leaders, stakeholders, and technology professionals
Strong analytical, conceptual, and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate complex and ambiguous business and technology issues, identify interdependencies, assess alternatives, and develop practical and sustainable solutions
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate complex technology concepts, risks, opportunities, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences
Demonstrated ability to lead complex organizational change and technology transformation initiatives while balancing strategic priorities, operational requirements, stakeholder needs, and organizational readiness

Job Description

Our client, a global leader in interactive entertainment, is seeking a Director of Player Experience (PX) Research to define and lead the future of player insight across a diverse, global portfolio.

This role sits at the intersection of research strategy, player understanding, and business impact. The Director will own the vision for PX Research, ensuring player insight informs decisions across the full lifecycle, from pre-production and early validation through live service and long-term ecosystem growth.

This leader will build and empower a high-performing research organization, partner closely with central Insights teams (Consumer Insights, Data & Analytics, Experience Quality, Fan Care), and drive clarity across emerging priorities such as new player acquisition, Gen Alpha, mobile strategy, and global market expansion.

This is a high-influence, transformation-oriented role, ideal for someone energized by scale, ambiguity, and shaping how research operates across a large organization.

Location: Canada or U.S.

Key Responsibilities

Research Strategy & Impact

Define and execute a global PX Research strategy that shapes the future of play across platforms, ecosystems, and franchises.
Ensure research delivers measurable impact on product strategy, portfolio decisions, and player outcomes.
Translate audience insights (TAM, SAM, SOM) into validated player cohorts that development teams can act on early, even pre-software.

Leadership & Culture

Lead and develop senior research leaders and ICs across regions and studios.
Foster a culture of curiosity, speed, and constructive challenge — enabling researchers to influence product direction.
Balance autonomy with alignment by establishing shared standards, frameworks, and expectations at scale.

Craft, Methodology & Tooling

Elevate PX research methodologies across qualitative, quantitative, telemetry, and sentiment inputs.
Advance experimentation, AI-assisted approaches, and integrated tooling to accelerate insight generation.
Oversee research vendors and external partners, including strategy for emerging markets.

Strategic Focus Areas

Build research approaches supporting:
New player acquisition and early playtesting pipelines
Gen Alpha and future player behaviors
Player sentiment integration with PX and Data
Sports research within fast (≈4-month) development cycles
Mobile PX strategy tied to HD franchises
Cloud, subscriptions, ecosystems, and eSports
APAC research strategy (short-term vendor execution + long-term presence)

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner deeply with Consumer Insights, Data & Analytics, Experience Quality, and Fan Care to deliver unified, non-siloed insights.
Deliver executive-ready narratives that connect player understanding to business and portfolio outcomes.
Support organizational change by bringing clarity, sequencing priorities, and sustaining momentum through transformation.

Qualifications

Degree in a relevant field (Psychology, HCI, Market Research, Social Sciences, Data Science) or equivalent industry experience.
10–12+ years in player research, UX research, or consumer insights, ideally within gaming or digital entertainment.
5+ years leading multi-disciplinary research teams at scale.
Strong fluency across mixed-methods research.
Demonstrated success influencing senior product and business leaders.
Experience operating in global, matrixed environments.
Comfortable shifting from hands-on product work to portfolio-level leadership.
Deep personal connection to players and the craft of research.

You can also earn up to $50,000 for helping us find new clients. jobs.title: VP Enterprise Marketing
jobs.description:
Mentimeter is an engagement company with a simple goal: to make every leader better. Through interaction, insights and recommendations, its platform helps organizations turn participation into better understanding and stronger performance.

Founded in Stockholm in 2012, Mentimeter is used by 20 million people each month across 1.3 million organizations. At Mentimeter, we believe better leadership starts with listening and that the strongest results are achieved together. That’s why we foster a culture built on curiosity, collaboration and shared ownership. By joining us, you’ll help leaders turn participation into deeper understanding and stronger performance, advancing our ambition to help more than one billion people listen, learn and work better together.

Build Mentimeter's enterprise growth engine

40 million users have experienced the value of using a Menti!

Building on that product-led foundation, Mentimeter is used daily by more than 84.000 organisations globally across all industries and we now serve more than 3,200 Enterprise customers globally. Our next challenge is to increase a systematic enterprise demand growth engine - and we are looking for a VP Enterprise Marketing to lead that journey.

This is a global leadership role responsible for how Mentimeter creates, identifies and converts enterprise demand. You will lead our Enterprise Marketing organisation, report to our Chief Sales Officer and join Mentimeter's Global Enterprise Leadership Team. Your primary focus will be EMEA and North America, while building the foundations for APAC. The goal is to connect our product adoption, organic reach and customer base into an Enterprise qualified pipeline, ARR and customer growth.

What You'll Lead

You will lead three existing teams, each with an experienced leader, across three connected areas:

Digital demand

Build and optimize enterprise demand generation and capture across web, paid media, account-based programs, content distribution, conversion and nurture.

Field and customer marketing

Develop a global strategy across events, partner programs, customer advocacy, regional activation and use-case storytelling - measured by account engagement, adoption, pipeline and expansion, not simply attendance.

Executive Exchange

Build Mentimeter's Executive Exchange into a distinctive platform for strategic customers, including our Enterprise Community, executive networks, education and certification programs.

What You'll Own

Define and own Mentimeter's global Enterprise Marketing strategy, budget and operating model.
Build an integrated system for demand generation and demand capture that turns our PLG footprint and product signals into account-level pipeline.
Set priorities across segments, accounts, audiences, buying groups, use cases and regions, balancing global consistency with local relevance.
Create qualified pipeline and measurable Enterprise ARR impact, with clear accountability for conversion, velocity, attribution and ROI.
Recruit, coach and develop leaders and senior marketing talent, creating an organisation that performs beyond your direct involvement.
Partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Product, Growth, Brand, Data and regional leadership to strengthen the handover from product-led growth to sales-assisted opportunities.
Stop, redesign or reallocate investment away from programs that do not create meaningful customer or commercial impact.

What Will Help You Succeed

You are an experienced B2B marketing leader who combines strategic range with commercial discipline. You are likely to bring:

12+ years of B2B SaaS marketing experience, including significant leadership experience in Enterprise Marketing, Demand Generation, Integrated Marketing or a closely related area.
Experience leading leaders and multidisciplinary teams across digital demand, field marketing, customer marketing or executive programs.
A strong understanding of enterprise buying journeys, account-based marketing, buying groups, demand capture and pipeline creation in a PLG environment.
Experience connecting product-led or high-volume inbound growth with a sales-assisted enterprise motion.
Commercial fluency across funnel economics, pipeline, conversion, attribution, investment and ROI.
Experience operating across EMEA and/or North America and adapting global programs to local markets.
An AI-native approach to marketing: using AI to improve insight, experimentation, personalisation and performance - not only individual productivity.

The Kind Of Leader Who Will Thrive Here

You create clarity where ownership is shared and the answer is not obvious. You set a high bar while building trust, develop leaders and give talented people meaningful ownership. Most importantly, you want to build - not simply inherit and administer - a modern Enterprise Marketing function, see the strategy through and be accountable for its long-term impact. You are ambitious while staying humble, curious and collaborative in how you get there.

Why this role

You will have the mandate to shape how Mentimeter approaches enterprise demand globally and define the next chapter of our Enterprise growth. If you are looking for a finished playbook, this probably is not the role for you. If you want to build the system and be accountable for its impact, we would like to hear from you.

We’re actively hiring for one position, which can be based in either Stockholm or Toronto. The role follows our hybrid way of working.

How We Lead At Mentimeter

At Mentimeter, we have a Leadership Manifesto that sets a shared direction for how we lead ourselves, our teams and the business. We call it Heart & Bravery.

It starts with authenticity: knowing yourself, showing yourself and leading yourself.

We expect our leaders to develop high-performing teams through both care and challenge, drive the right results in a changing environment, and set a clear direction by connecting the work to our vision and making the complex simple.

You will learn more about our Leadership Manifesto throughout the recruitment process. These principles are also an important part of how we assess and hire leaders at Mentimeter.

Our recruitment process

We Want The Process To Be Transparent And Give Both You And Us The Opportunity To Get To Know Each Other Properly. The Steps Are

TA Intro Interview
Hiring Manager Interview: A 20-minute digital chat with our Chief Sales Officer to meet and learn more about the role
Business Case & Competence Interview
A short business case, submitted the day before the competence interview
Competence interview: 75-minute at our office

Leadership and culture interview: 90-minute at our office
References and a coffee chat with the team
Offer and signing

Compensation

At Mentimeter, we believe in fair and transparent compensation that grows with you. The annual base salary range for this role is $226,000–$303,000 CAD. It’s intentionally broad to reflect different stages of growth within the role: from growing into its full scope to bringing deep expertise and meaningful impact from day one.

Where an individual is placed within the range depends on factors such as relevant experience, demonstrated skills, and alignment with the role’s requirements. We’re committed to supporting your growth. You’ll have ongoing development conversations with your manager, and your compensation will be reviewed as your skills, scope and impact evolve.

In addition to your salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits package - learn more about it here: https://www.mentimeter.com/benefits/toronto .

What Mentimeter Can Offer

At Mentimeter we can offer a diverse and inclusive work environment supported by smart and driven colleagues. We believe in continuous professional development for all of our colleagues and therefore offer access to a leadership program (including external personal coach) and relevant education to ensure that we continue to be state-of-the-art when it comes to innovating and building Mentimeter. Your place will be in a growing company with lots of career opportunities, working on a beloved product used by more than 300 million people. It’s not all about work though, we also offer a very healthy view on work-life balance.

All of this comes attached with a competitive compensation and benefits package, including pension contributions. Learn more about our benefits by visiting our Benefits & Perks page

AI and Hiring at Mentimeter

At Mentimeter, we believe AI helps us work smarter - but it never replaces the human assessment, curiosity, and personal connection that define our culture and our hiring. We use AI as a sparring partner: to bounce ideas, bring new perspectives, support structure, and make our work more efficient. But the meaning, decisions, and interactions always come from people. AI strengthens our work, but it does not define it. At Mentimeter, we’re not building an AI-driven hiring process - we’re building a people-first culture, where technology helps us listen, learn, and grow together.

Culture at Mentimeter

At Mentimeter we believe in giving everyone a voice - regardless of who you are. So we build a platform that does just that. Our platform is not only our product but also our organization. A platform where people feel safe, where differences are embraced, a place where you can have fun. We strongly encourage applicants who are people of color, LGBTQ+, women, people with disabilities, and/or formerly incarcerated people, and a college degree is not strictly required. In order to give everyone a voice, we need to be as diverse as our users.

Learn more about our culture by visiting our Culture page.

Review our Privacy Policy for more information.

The Managing Director will provide strategic, commercial, and operational leadership for Halliwell, driving sustainable growth, technical excellence, and client satisfaction across its multidisciplinary consulting and technical advisory services.
Halliwell partners with clients to navigate complex damage, failures, and recovery challenges. Through independent, unbiased technical evaluations and practical, cost-certain repair and replacement strategies, the business delivers the clarity and confidence clients need to make informed decisions and restore functionality.

The Managing Director will lead the execution of Halliwell’s business strategy, strengthen its market position, develop high-performing multidisciplinary teams, and build lasting relationships with clients, industry partners, insurers, legal professionals, and other key stakeholders. This individual will ensure that Halliwell continues to deliver high-quality, evidence-based advice that bridges the gap between complex damage and functional recovery.

Identify new markets, service opportunities, and strategic partnerships to strengthen Halliwell’s competitive position.

new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

Reporting to the Associate Vice-Principal, Finance and Administration, the Executive Director, Integrated Finance Services is accountable, within delegated authority, for the performance and coherence of the function as a whole. The Executive Director leads the development and implementation of the function’s strategy and operating model, aligned with AVP direction and approved enterprise-wide Finance strategy, and is accountable for cross-portfolio capacity and risk management, consistent service standards and controls, and the performance and development of Integrated Finance Services Directors.

The Executive Director ensures Directors have the approved frameworks, delegated authority, capability and support required to lead their portfolios or managed groups effectively and exercise their authority without unnecessary approval layers. Faculty, shared services and portfolio leaders remain accountable for academic and operational priorities, business and staffing decisions, budget approval, corrective business action and resource allocation within their delegated authorities. Integrated Finance Services supports these decisions through analysis, advice, controls and implementation of approved decisions.

The Executive Director becomes directly involved when matters exceed an individual Director’s delegated authority, require decisions across Director-led groups, remain unresolved following Director-level action, or have institutional financial, control, service or strategic implications. The Executive Director resolves matters within delegated authority and escalates institutional determinations to the AVP.

As a senior member of the Finance leadership team, the Executive Director advises the AVP on service performance, capacity, capability, risk and improvement priorities, coordinates implementation of approved Finance initiatives and represents Integrated Finance Services in designated institutional, regulatory and external forums.

The AVP, Finance and Administration retains institutional professional and people accountability for Integrated Finance Services, including enterprise-wide strategy, service standards, workforce performance and institutional service expectations. The Executive Director exercises delegated leadership and management authority within this framework.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Finance Services Leadership and Operating Model

Leads the development, implementation and continuous improvement of the Integrated Finance Services strategy and operating model, aligned with AVP direction and approved enterprise-wide Finance strategy.
Directs and oversees Integrated Finance Services activities and ensures alignment with University financial policies and AVP direction.
Develops and recommends Integrated Finance Services standards, operating practices, performance measures and escalation protocols for AVP approval, and implements them across Director-led areas.
Monitors Finance service delivery, quality, responsiveness, capacity utilization and client outcomes across all portfolios and directs corrective action at the Director level where required.
Resolves cross-portfolio and cross-Director service, capacity, priority and accountability conflicts and makes function-wide Finance capacity and service trade-off decisions within approved budgets, workforce plans, service expectations and delegated authority.
Determines when direct Executive Director involvement is warranted based on institutional materiality, strategic significance, cross-portfolio impact, unresolved Director-level matters or escalation requirements.

Service Performance and Standards

Maintains visibility of Finance performance across Director led groups and brings material service failures, systemic issues, structural capacity shortfalls and emerging risks to the AVP with recommended action.
Maintains relationships with designated institutional leaders to understand service expectations and identify systemic concerns, while preserving Director and Senior Manager ownership of principal portfolio Finance relationships.
Conducts periodic service reviews, using service data, client feedback, audit findings and Director-provided intelligence to identify trends, gaps and opportunities for improvement.
Develops, maintains and continuously improves the approved Integrated Finance Services performance framework and recommends changes to the AVP where needed.
Holds Directors accountable for applying approved service standards and for taking timely corrective action.
Maintains an integrated view of financial, control and service risks across Director led groups, identifies systemic issues and institutional implications, and coordinates appropriate Finance responses. Escalates institutional-level financial matters to the AVP with analysis and recommended action.
Provides timely advice to the AVP on institutional level financial pressures, structural risks and recommended responses. Supports accountable client leaders through analysis, advice and implementation support where corrective business action is required.

Capacity and Resource Management

Coordinates deployment of Finance capacity across Director-led groups and makes cross-portfolio deployment decisions within approved workforce plans, budgets and delegated authority.
Balances available capacity across all Director-led groups and makes transparent service and workload trade-offs within delegated authority.
Identifies structural capacity pressures, coordinates available responses and recommends longer-term resource or organizational changes to the AVP.
Maintains oversight of Finance workforce structure, succession risk and organizational effectiveness and advises the AVP on significant workforce or organizational design matters.

People Leadership and Finance Capability

Provides leadership, direction and coaching to Directors and establishes clear performance and accountability expectations across the Finance leadership group.
Conducts performance reviews for Directors and obtains relevant client input on integrated service delivery and relationship effectiveness.
Makes decisions and recommendations concerning the Integrated Finance Services workforce, including recruitment, workforce planning, performance, development, discipline and organization design within delegated authority.
Builds leadership capability and resilience through coaching, professional development, succession planning, and cross-portfolio knowledge sharing.
Sets Finance capability expectations and sponsors coordinated development initiatives across the function.
Fosters, promotes and drives equity and inclusion.

Transformation and Institutional Contribution

Leads implementation of approved Finance Services transformation, process standardization, automation and service-improvement priorities across Director-led areas.
Contributes to Finance governance and policy development and leads implementation of approved standards and policies across Finance Services.
Leads or sponsors implementation of significant Finance systems, operating-model changes and transformation programs and monitors adoption, performance and realization of intended benefits.
Represents approved Finance Services priorities, capabilities and accountabilities in institutional forums and external networks.
Identifies opportunities to improve the value, consistency and effectiveness of Finance Services and recommends material changes to the AVP.
Other duties as required in support of the department and/or unit.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

University degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance or a related field.
Chartered Professional Accountant designation or equivalent recognized professional accounting designation.
Minimum 10 years of senior leadership experience in financial management, planning, reporting, people leadership, operations and advisory services within a large, complex organization.
Demonstrated experience leading multiple Finance service areas or portfolios through senior leaders and coordinating consistent service delivery across a large, complex organization.
Proven experience advising and influencing senior and executive leaders on significant financial, service, risk and organizational matters.
Extensive experience with institutional budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, enterprise reporting, internal controls, risk management and diverse and complex funding or revenue structures.
Demonstrated experience leading major organizational change, operating-model transformation and implementation of large-scale Finance systems and practices.
Experience in a university, public-sector, health-sector, research-intensive or similarly complex multi-client environment is strongly preferred.
Criminal Sector Check required.
Consideration will be given to an equivalent combination of education and experience.

SPECIAL SKILLS:

Comprehensive knowledge of Finance strategy development and implementation, institutional governance, enterprise risk, organizational planning and integrated Finance service delivery at scale.
Systems-level thinking with the ability to integrate information from multiple portfolios into coherent advice, options and recommendations.
Superior relationship-building, influencing and communication skills, including the ability to provide objective, professional challenge to senior leaders.
Advanced financial-management, forecasting, analytical and risk assessment skills.
Ability to lead through a Director level management layer while balancing functional coherence with appropriate portfolio autonomy.
Sound judgement in determining when AVP, executive or governing-body escalation is required.
Proven success developing and implementing strategic plans and meeting objectives.
Proven management and leadership experience with a demonstrated ability to organize, motivate and influence within and outside of direct span of control.
Demonstrated ability to effectively build and manage partner relationships that enhance and advance the interests of the University.
Proven ability to collaboratively develop a future vision of program initiative goals and needs, champion this vision, and secure and/or coordinate the resources to pursue associated goals.
Demonstrated ability to mentor, inspire others, articulate aspirational goals and institutional priorities, and effectively support new program initiatives.
Fosters a diverse and inclusive work environment where there is mutual respect and collaboration across all teams.
A strategic, innovative, and collaborative leader who successfully seeks out and fosters collaboration and partnerships in a complex multi-stakeholder environment.

DECISION MAKING:

Leads the development of Integrated Finance Services strategy and recommends it to the AVP for approval; determines functional priorities, operating plans and implementation requirements within approved enterprise-wide strategy and delegated authority.
Coordinates cross-portfolio deployment of approved Finance capacity and makes material workload decisions within delegated authority; recommends significant structural or resource changes to the AVP.
Resolves cross-Director matters and determines when AVP escalation is required.
Makes material Integrated Finance Services decisions on delivery, controls, capacity, organizational design and risk within delegated authority.
Advises the AVP on significant financial matters; final academic, operational and resource-allocation decisions remain with the appropriately authorized leader.
Coordinates consistent interpretation and application of financial policy across Finance Services, establishes operating practices within approved frameworks and escalates policy matters requiring institutional determination to the AVP or appropriate authority.

new_jobs.description:
Talan is an international group that supports its clients in their end-to-end Data & AI transformation by combining management consulting with technological expertise.

With over 6,000 employees across five continents, we accelerate our clients' transformations through long-term partnerships, creating measurable and sustainable impact.

Our value proposition is built on a structured innovation ecosystem: 2,500 Data & AI experts, proprietary solutions built on advanced models, and an applied research, experimental development, and innovation laboratory.

In Americas, our multidisciplinary teams bring over 30 years of experience helping business leaders across key industries achieve measurable performance and strong ROI, designing, building, and scaling solutions that enable companies to grow more efficiently.

Job Description

Reporting to the Senior Director, SAP Presales and Alliance, the SAP Customer Solution Director is part of the SAP practice and serves as the functional design authority for clients and delivery teams. The role maintains solution continuity from the earliest pursuit and presales discussions through delivery, user acceptance testing, go-live and support, helping ensure that the solution sold remains consistent with the solution designed and delivered.

Working at the intersection of business development, presales and delivery, you translate complex business challenges into an SAP solution that can be built, estimated and aligned with the client’s industry. You own process design and the industry response, while technical architecture remains with the Solution Architect or Enterprise Architect and execution, staffing and margin remain with project management and delivery leadership. Your influence, judgement and deep SAP S/4HANA knowledge contribute directly to client satisfaction and sales growth.

Your mission consists of:

Client orientation and business value:
Lead functional solutioning for pursuits, requests for proposal and oral presentations by translating client business problems into an SAP solution that Talan can estimate and deliver.
Build and defend the value case with business stakeholders, including benefit drivers, baseline measures and the operational changes required to realize the expected value.
Advise decision-makers and, when appropriate, recommend a no-bid decision when industry fit or client readiness does not support a responsible proposal.

Business development and influence:
Define solution assumptions, scope boundaries, exclusions and functional inputs to estimates, then challenge estimates before they are incorporated into pricing.
Design and present, with Alliance and Presales teams, industry-relevant demonstrations, accelerators and proof-of-concept scenarios.
Support joint pursuits, industry positioning and engagement with SAP account teams and ecosystem partners.

Design leadership and risk management:
Act as the functional design authority, decide on process design and fit-to-standard matters, and chair or co-chair workshops focused on critical processes.
Provide a documented transition from the sold solution to the delivery team, including the assumption register, scope baseline and design intent.
Serve as an escalation point when scope, industry fit or process design is at risk, and support the rationale for required changes.

Delivery excellence:
Review and approve process design deliverables before they are submitted to the client for sign-off.
Validate the delivered design against the original value case through user acceptance testing, go-live and stabilization.
Advise the team on organizational impacts arising from process design in partnership with the change management lead.

Collaboration and practice development:
Coach functional consultants and domain leads to strengthen the team’s ability to hold credible industry conversations with clients.
Advance the industry intellectual property roadmap, including process models, configuration accelerators, demo scenarios and client references.
Feed delivery lessons into leads, packaged offerings, accelerators and the process content used by AI-enabled delivery tools.

Qualifications

Experience
: Nine (9) to twelve (12) years of relevant SAP experience in functional, solution design or process architecture roles.
SAP delivery record
: Participation in at least four full-cycle SAP implementations, including at least two as a functional lead or solution owner.
Industry expertise
: Deep experience in the industry named in the posting and command of its associated end-to-end processes.
SAP S/4HANA
: At least three (3) years of experience with current S/4HANA releases in public or private cloud, including demonstrated fit-to-standard practice.
Estimating and delivery
: Demonstrated experience defining assumptions, scope and effort estimates that a delivery team was accountable for executing.
Executive advisory
: Experience leading oral presentations, executive workshops and value discussions with VP- or C-level business stakeholders.
Education
: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Supply Chain, Information Technology or a related field.
Conditions
: Ability to travel to client sites in Canada and the United-States; travel may represent 30% to 50% of working time during pursuit and design phases.
Communication
: Good oral and written communication skills, in French and English, to communicate with clients located across North America.

Experience in the specific industry vertical aligned to the role, with a strong understanding of end-to-end business processes and industry-specific SAP solutions.

Mining
:

Mine-to-cash end to end, including ore movement, production reporting, and cost per tonne
Plant maintenance, asset management, MRO, and warehouse for asset-intensive operations
Concentrate and commodity sales, including provisional pricing and weight and assay settlement
Royalties, offtake agreements, and shipment reconciliation
Integration boundaries with mine planning, fleet management, and metallurgical accounting systems

Well-to-wallet end to end

Joint venture accounting and production revenue accounting

Secondary distribution and downstream logistics processes

Demand planning and S&OP
Trade promotion planning, execution, settlement, deductions, and claims
Revenue growth management and pricing and rebate structures
Customer Activity Repository and demand data foundation
DSD, batch traceability, quality management, and recall readiness
Retailer EDI, GS1 standards, and allocation under constrained supply

Plan-to-produce end to end
Engineer-to-order and configure-to-order flows, including variant configuration
Production planning and detailed scheduling, and MRP in S/4HANA
Quality management and non-conformance handling
Service parts, warranty, and installed base
Project systems on capital work and long-cycle manufacturing

Generous employer contributions to your group RRSP.
